text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ADEVARUL
- Shortage of funds prevent backeries from buying wheat.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Investors are reluctant to put their money in the companies shortlisted for privatisation, the paper says.
- State-run Tarom airline is affected by a serious shortage of funds, the paper says.
- The state-run Giurgiu free trade zone will call a tender to lease land and buildings.
- The National Oil Company will undergo a restructuring programme, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Telephone operator Romtelecom RA plans to raise tariffs starting June 1.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- A family can own up to 200 hectares of farmland according to a new bill passed by parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton, in a speach in The Hague, praised Romania for its democratic progress and for inviting representatives of the country's ethnic Hungarians to be part of the centrist government elected last year.
ADEVARUL
- MPs of the ruling coalition member Democratic Party (PD) plan to boycott the government's draft laws if they are them inconsistent with the PD's views.

- The opposition Party of Social Democracy's no-confidence motion will be debated by the parliament on June 3. It is the first such motion against the centrist government of Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Washington and London exclude Romania from the first wave of a planned NATO expansion, the newspaper says commenting on statements by American and British officials at Sintra, Portugal, at a NATO conference.

- The ceremony of signing the Romanian-Ukrainian friendship treaty will take place at the summer holiday house of former Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu in the Black Sea coast resort of Neptun. ($ = 7,114 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
